objects: unordered set of points {P1,...,Pn} in R^m
assumptions: input is an unordered set and the network must be invariant to permutation of points
the learned representation should be robust to rigid transformations such as rotation and translation
guarantees: formal theorem: shared per-point transformation plus max pooling can approximate any continuous set function arbitrarily well
formal theorem: the network output is determined by a bounded critical point set
empirical only for actual classification/segmentation accuracy
formalism.operation: shared MLP applied identically to every point, followed by symmetric element-wise max pooling over all points to produce a global feature

evidence_spans.objects: A point cloud is represented as a set of 3D points {Pi | i = 1, ..., n}, where each point Pi is a vector of its (x, y, z) coordinate plus extra feature channels.
evidence_spans.assumptions: a network that consumes N 3D point sets needs to be invariant to N! permutations of the input set in data feeding order.
